title: CastillosBurstVEP40
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 12 healthy participants performing a reactive brain-computer interface task using code-modulated visual evoked potentials (c-VEP). The study introduces an innovative 'Burst c-VEP' paradigm employing short bursts of aperiodic visual flashes at 2-4 Hz, designed to optimize classification performance while reducing calibration requirements and improving visual comfort. Data were collected using a 32-channel BrainProducts LiveAmp system at 500 Hz sampling rate across a factorial design manipulating stimulus pattern (burst vs. m-sequence) and amplitude (100% vs. 40% depth modulation).
methods_description: EEG data were acquired from 12 healthy participants (mean age 30.6±7.1 years) using a 32-channel BrainProducts LiveAmp system with active Acticap electrodes at a sampling rate of 500 Hz. The experimental protocol employed a factorial design with four conditions: burst or m-sequence codes crossed with 100% or 40% amplitude depth modulations. Participants attended to sequentially cued targets presented as aperiodic visual flashes on a Dell P2419HC display (1920×1080 pixels, 60 Hz refresh rate). Each participant completed 15 blocks of 4 trials per condition (240 total trials). Burst codes consisted of 50ms flashes at 2-4 Hz with 200ms minimum inter-burst intervals, while m-sequences used pseudo-random binary sequences at ~10 Hz. EEG signals were processed using convolutional neural networks for bitwise decoding.
